sentences.text: The holotype specimen of Leurospondylus ultimus was a juvenile animal.
The specific name ultimus means 'last' because the genus represented the latest known fossil plesiosaur at the time of its description in 1913.
Samuel Paul Welles noted that the vertebrae resemble those of pliosaurs while the shoulder bones resemble those of elasmosaurids, making family classification difficult.
The genus Leurospondylus was described by Brown in 1913.
The fossils were found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada, within the brackish Edmonton beds of the present-day Red Deer River.

The family of Leurospondylus is disputed, though it is suggested to belong to Elasmosauridae, while some sources suggest it belongs to the family Plesiosauridae, though this is disputed. The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Leurospondylus as Elasmosauridae.
Leurospondylus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
It is unknown whether Leurospondylus grew up and left the freshwater ecosystem or remained there as an adult.
It is debated whether the Leurospondylus specimen is a juvenile of a known species or belongs to an unrecognized taxonomic group.
